newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sets tender for 2-year, 3.50 pct notes.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sets tender for 2-year, 3.50 pct notes.

text.p: The German federal government set an auction on Tuesday for two-year 3.50 percent coupon Treasury notes with bids due by 1000 GMT on Wednesday, the Bundesbank said.
The bond matures on December 18, 1998 and the first interest payment will be made on December 18, 1997.
The Bundesbank, who is the issuing agent, said the payment date will be December 20 and that the notes will be listed on the bourse on December 23.
Germany has pledged to issue two-year notes at quarterly auctions as part of a package of measures to aid the development of the domestic bond market by selling more short-term government debt.
The government in July, for the first time, sold six-month Treasury bills, or Bubills.
